findings.title: Public Today/market-board reads recompute the whole board per request; one function loaded every odds snapshot ever recorded for each game
findings.evidence: REPRODUCED. Warm, concurrency 1, live DB: /today?date=2026-09-02 8.2-9.3 s; /markets/board 7.2-8.4 s; /performance 4.4-4.9 s. Instrumented: dashboard(15 games) = 509 SQL queries, 785 ms SQL, 6.5 s Python. cProfile: ReadService._latest_market_snapshots 30 calls, 8.0 s cumulative, 258,974 ORM instances materialised (2,160 snapshot rows per game x 4 entities, called up to 3x per game).
findings.reproduction: python scratch qcount.py / prof.py (SQLAlchemy cursor-event counter + cProfile around ReadService.dashboard(date(2026,9,2))) against a read-only session on the live database.
findings.impact: Landing-page p50 ~9 s at ONE user. Under c=8 the same request serialises to 62 s (0.13 rps). Trivially abusable as CPU denial of service via ?date=.
findings.rootCause: _latest_market_snapshots selected all (Market, MarketOutcome, OddsSnapshot, Sportsbook) rows for a game ordered by observed_at and reduced 'latest batch per (market, sportsbook)' in Python; no per-request memo; no response cache.
findings.remediation: REPAIRED: reduction expressed in SQL (GROUP BY market_id, sportsbook_id -> MAX(observed_at) subquery join) with cutoff/source_mode pushed into SQL and a per-ReadService memo. Verified equivalent to a verbatim copy of the old reducer. REMAINING (RECOMMENDED): evidence-versioned response cache for public reads, bounded ?date= window, composite index odds_snapshots(market_outcome_id, observed_at DESC), separate scheduler process.
tests: server/tests/test_fable51_latest_market_snapshots.py (4 tests: exact equivalence vs reference reducer, cutoff parity, memoisation, only winning rows fetched)
findings.residualRisk: After repair, measured on an idle machine: /today?date=2026-09-02 1.6 s p50 at c=1 (was 9.1 s), still GIL-serialised at c=8 (11.4 s p50, 0.69 rps; was 62 s / 0.13 rps); /markets/board 307 ms (was 7-8 s); /performance unchanged at ~4.2 s. Not acceptable for public reads without the evidence-versioned cache/read-model.

findings.title: Scheduler jobs execute on the API event loop and freeze every HTTP request for their duration
findings.evidence: REPRODUCED: /sports/registry (3 ms warm) showed p99 28,439 ms at c=1 and p95 53,216 ms at c=16 while freeze-shadow-experiment / finalize-games / poll-availability-events fired (backend log 16:16-16:21Z); the same endpoint ran 114 rps p95 769 ms when no job was running. OBSERVED: AsyncIOScheduler runs `async def execute_scheduled_job` on the app loop; handlers do sync DB/CPU work inline; no run_in_threadpool/to_thread anywhere in app/jobs or app/services.
findings.reproduction: scratch bench.py concurrency sweep during scheduled job windows.
findings.impact: Periodic multi-second to minute-long API freezes every 2-5 minutes; horizontal scaling impossible (each replica would also run the scheduler).
findings.rootCause: Scheduler embedded in the API process (`lifespan`), coroutine jobs blocking the loop.
findings.remediation: RECOMMENDED (architecture plan §2.1/§5): standalone scheduler process (`SCHEDULER_ENABLED=false` on API replicas), advisory-lock leader lease, job-window unique key in job_runs. Not implemented in this audit because it changes the operator's runtime topology; the code split is small.

findings.title: Missed 06:00 daily pipeline is never caught up; a dead process across the cron fire yields a silent zero-slate day
findings.evidence: REPRODUCED in live data: job_runs has no daily-pipeline row for 2026-09-03 (process died 21:12 EDT on 9/2, restarted 11:46 EDT on 9/3); games for 2026-09-03 = 0, forecasts generated = 0; Today page showed 'No slate on this operational date'. misfire_grace_time=900 s cannot cover a 5.5 h outage.
findings.reproduction: SELECT ... FROM job_runs WHERE job_name='daily-pipeline' grouped by local date; days 08-21..08-27 and 09-03 absent.
findings.impact: A dead-scheduler day is indistinguishable from an honest no-bet day; the mandate classifies this as an operational failure.
findings.rootCause: Cron-only registration with a 15-minute misfire grace and no startup reconciliation.
findings.remediation: REPAIRED: daily_pipeline_catch_up_time() schedules one immediate first fire at scheduler start when local time is past 06:00 and no SUCCEEDED daily-pipeline exists for the local date; fails safe to cron on any bookkeeping error; cron cadence unchanged afterwards. RECOMMENDED: alert 'no daily-pipeline success by 07:00 local'.
tests: server/tests/test_fable51_scheduler_reliability.py (9 catch-up tests incl. ET day boundary, FAILED-run today, disabled scheduler, fail-safe, cron untouched)
findings.residualRisk: Catch-up still runs inside the API process until F51-002 is addressed.

findings.title: evaluate-prediction-market-alerts fails on an in-batch duplicate idempotency key and discards every alert (286 of 332 runs failed in 3 days)
findings.evidence: REPRODUCED: live job_runs: evaluate-prediction-market-alerts FAILED x286 / SUCCEEDED x46 (72 h) with UniqueViolation uq_pm_alert_idempotency; log parameters show the identical key twice within one INSERT batch. Regression test fails on original code with 'UNIQUE constraint failed: prediction_market_alerts.idempotency_key' and passes after the fix.
findings.impact: Alerts feature silently non-functional ~86% of the time; wasted DB work every 10 minutes.
findings.likelihood: Certain whenever two lines exist for one selection.
findings.rootCause: _latest_snapshots_by_provider keys by (provider, market, selection, line_value) but the alert key omits line_value; _exists() cannot see pending rows under autoflush=False.
findings.remediation: REPAIRED: observer tracks idempotency keys added in the current batch and treats an in-batch duplicate as a no-op (key semantics unchanged). RECOMMENDED: alert on >=3 consecutive failures of any job.

findings.title: Operational backend runs as an unsupervised foreground process; it died twice during the audit week and nothing restarted it
findings.evidence: OBSERVED: process on :8010 started 8/31 14:02 with no supervisor; died 9/2 16:20 and again 9/2 21:12 (logs end mid-job, no shutdown line, no crash, no reboot, no OS error). REPRODUCED consequence: F51-003.
findings.reproduction: Windows event log + backend logs + job_runs timeline.
findings.impact: Any termination = no API, no scheduler, missed pipeline, stuck RUNNING rows.
findings.rootCause: No service/supervisor; Task Scheduler registration from a non-elevated session cannot launch (Interactive tasks return result 1; S4U/Group require elevation).
findings.remediation: MITIGATED: restart-loop supervisor script at C:\Users\james\AppData\Local\asp\start-backend.cmd (currently running). RECOMMENDED: register it at logon (Startup entry or an elevated Scheduled Task with RestartCount) - exact commands in the master report; production: managed container platform with health-gated restarts and /readyz.
findings.residualRisk: Still dies with the session that started it until the user installs the logon entry.

findings.title: JobRun rows killed mid-execution stay RUNNING forever (impossible status surfaced as 'running')
findings.evidence: OBSERVED in live DB: 4 rows RUNNING since 08-30..09-01 (refresh-prediction-market-snapshots x2, finalize-prediction-market-pregame, freeze-shadow-experiment).
findings.reproduction: SELECT job_name, started_at FROM job_runs WHERE status='running' AND started_at < now()-interval '1 hour'.
findings.impact: Operators cannot distinguish a wedged job from a killed process; missed-run detection is poisoned.
findings.rootCause: Terminal status only written by the orchestrator's own try/except; no startup reconciliation.
findings.remediation: REPAIRED: reconcile_abandoned_job_runs() at scheduler start marks RUNNING rows FAILED with 'ABANDONED: process restarted before the job completed' (single-process topology; must become lease-aware for replicas - documented).
findings.residualRisk: Not replica-safe by design; see architecture plan §5.

findings.title: No unauthenticated readiness probe; /healthz never checked the database or scheduler
findings.evidence: OBSERVED: /healthz returns static ok; /health and /health/sources require ADMIN, so a load balancer/supervisor could not gate traffic.
findings.impact: Supervisors and LBs route to wedged/unready instances.
findings.remediation: REPAIRED: GET /readyz -> 200 {status, database, scheduler} or 503; booleans only, no quota/credentials.
tests: server/tests/test_fable51_scheduler_reliability.py (3 probe tests incl. 503 on DB failure and no error-detail leakage)

findings.title: SQLAlchemy pool (5+10) smaller than the 40-slot request threadpool; 30 s pool_timeout queues instead of failing fast
findings.evidence: OBSERVED: _engine_options returned only pool_pre_ping; live max_connections=100, 9 active.
findings.impact: Pool waits under >15 concurrent DB-bound requests.
findings.remediation: REPAIRED: DB_POOL_SIZE (10), DB_MAX_OVERFLOW (20), DB_POOL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (10) settings applied for PostgreSQL; SQLite unchanged. RECOMMENDED: PgBouncer + statement_timeout in production.
findings.residualRisk: Per-replica sizing must respect PostgreSQL max_connections.

findings.title: Process-local state blocks multi-replica deployment: rate-limit counters, scheduler ownership flags, job max_instances, per-request caches
findings.evidence: OBSERVED: InMemoryRateLimiter module global; _SCHEDULER_RUNNING/_SCHEDULER_INSTANCE globals; APScheduler memory jobstore; documented in code as single-instance only.
findings.impact: Replica N multiplies scheduled work and provider spend; rate limits per replica.
findings.remediation: RECOMMENDED: Redis-backed limiter; scheduler as its own service with advisory-lock lease; job-window unique key.

findings.title: No PostgreSQL backup, no WAL archiving, no restore evidence
findings.evidence: OBSERVED: archive_mode=off, archive_command disabled; no pg_dump/backup script in repo; host scheduled tasks named 'Backup' are Windows OS tasks (AppListBackup, CloudRestore, RegIdleBackup).
findings.impact: Irreplaceable immutable experiment history (positions, decisions, forecasts since 2026-08-27) has RPO = infinity.
findings.remediation: RECOMMENDED: nightly pg_dump -Fc to off-host storage + WAL archiving/PITR; quarterly restore drill; managed PostgreSQL in production.

findings.title: Provider-key scratch file (SportsDataIO.txt) sits in the repo root, untracked and not git-ignored
findings.evidence: OBSERVED: notepad.exe had C:\Users\james\ai-sports-predictor\SportsDataIO.txt open; `git check-ignore` reported NOT ignored; not tracked; never in history.
findings.impact: One `git add .` commits a paid API key.
findings.remediation: REPAIRED: ignore patterns for /SportsDataIO*.txt and /*api-key*.txt style files. RECOMMENDED: keep keys only in .env / secret manager.

findings.title: Development listeners on all interfaces: Vite 0.0.0.0:5173, PostgreSQL 0.0.0.0:5432; runtime is APP_ENV=development with DEMO_MODE=true
findings.evidence: OBSERVED: Get-NetTCPConnection listeners; package.json `vite --host 0.0.0.0`; .env APP_ENV=development, DEMO_MODE=true.
findings.impact: LAN exposure of a dev server and the database; production validators (secret, CORS, docs, HSTS) are all bypassed in development mode.
findings.likelihood: Depends on network; certain misconfiguration risk if ever port-forwarded.
findings.remediation: RECOMMENDED: bind to 127.0.0.1 locally; production behind TLS proxy with APP_ENV=production; DEMO_MODE=false (validator enforces).
findings.residualRisk: Must be closed before any public exposure.

findings.title: Open registration without email verification, password reset, breached-password screening, per-account lockout, or MFA
findings.evidence: OBSERVED: RegisterRequest min_length=12 only (code comment: BREACHED_PASSWORD_CHECK_REQUIRED_BEFORE_PUBLIC_PRODUCTION); no reset/verify routes; per-IP limiter only.
findings.impact: Account-recovery impossible; credential stuffing against a specific account limited only by per-IP counters.
findings.remediation: RECOMMENDED before public beta: email verification, reset flow, k-anonymity HIBP check, per-account lockout, Redis limiter; MFA for ADMIN.
findings.residualRisk: Acceptable only for an invited cohort.

findings.title: Immutability of positions/settlements/decisions is enforced only at the ORM layer
findings.evidence: OBSERVED: before_flush listeners; one DB trigger exists (trg_prospective_label_access_complete_claim) proving the pattern; none on ledger tables; single DB role.
findings.impact: Raw SQL, another client, or a migration can rewrite history undetected.
findings.remediation: RECOMMENDED: BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE triggers raising on ledger tables; role split (app/read-only/migrate).

findings.title: No CI pipeline; no Python lockfile; container runs as root and runs migrations + create-admin at start; compose hard-codes DB password
findings.evidence: OBSERVED: no .github; requirements.txt ranges; Dockerfile no USER; compose POSTGRES_PASSWORD <redacted>.
findings.impact: No automated gate; irreproducible builds; privilege and secret hygiene gaps in the only deployment artefact.
findings.remediation: RECOMMENDED: CI (pytest, vitest, tsc, pip-audit, npm audit, build); pip-compile lockfile with hashes; non-root USER; release-step migrations.

findings.title: No metrics, no alerting; job failures visible only to an admin reading /admin/jobs
findings.evidence: OBSERVED: structlog JSON to stdout only; the 286-failure alert bug ran for days unnoticed; refresh-prediction-market-snapshots reports errors:122 with job_completed.
findings.impact: Silent degradation.
findings.remediation: RECOMMENDED: metrics + alert set in architecture plan §2.5; request-id middleware.

findings.title: No request body size limit at the application layer
findings.evidence: OBSERVED grep: no size-limit middleware; pydantic bounds field lengths but the body is read first.
findings.impact: Memory pressure from oversized POSTs.
findings.remediation: RECOMMENDED: proxy client_max_body_size 64k; optional Content-Length middleware.

findings.title: Registration reveals whether an email exists (409 Conflict)
findings.evidence: OBSERVED: DuplicateEmailError -> 409 with message.
findings.impact: Account enumeration (login is already safe).
findings.remediation: RECOMMENDED: with email verification, respond 202 uniformly.

findings.title: npm: echarts <6.1.0 moderate advisory (fix available); pip: pytest 8.4.2 PYSEC-2026-1845 (dev-only, UNIX /tmp)
findings.evidence: REPRODUCED: npm audit (1 moderate); pip-audit (1 advisory in 56 packages).
findings.impact: Not exploitable in this app's production shape.
findings.remediation: RECOMMENDED: upgrade echarts in a change window; pytest is dev-only.

findings.title: Pages fetch once and never retry; a momentary API blip leaves the page in a permanent error state; registry cached for app lifetime
findings.evidence: OBSERVED code; REPRODUCED on 9/2 and 9/3 (page stuck on 'unavailable' after backend recovered until manual reload).
findings.impact: Users see outages longer than they last.
findings.remediation: RECOMMENDED: bounded exponential retry + visibility-change refetch; registry refetch on failure.

findings.title: vitest 5 s default timeout is too tight on this machine for jsdom route tests (6 failures under load, all pass at 30 s)
findings.evidence: REPRODUCED: 6 failed / 116 passed concurrently with server suite; 4 failed in isolation at 5 s; 29/29 passed with --testTimeout=30000.
findings.impact: Flaky CI signal.
findings.remediation: RECOMMENDED: testTimeout 15-20 s in vitest config.

findings.title: Moneyline tie (equal final scores) settles as LOSS rather than PUSH/VOID
findings.evidence: OBSERVED: determine_result returns WIN if selected_score > opponent_score else LOSS.
findings.impact: MLB regular-season ties are effectively impossible (suspended games resume); relevant only if the sport set grows (NFL ties exist).
findings.likelihood: Very low for MLB; real for NFL.
findings.remediation: RECOMMENDED: explicit PUSH on equality before any non-MLB funded market.

findings.title: Unbounded growth of append-only snapshot/log tables with no retention or partitioning
findings.evidence: OBSERVED: odds_snapshots 173k rows (66 MB), prediction_market_* 159k rows (~200 MB), job_runs 8.4k, audit_events 8.4k in ~3 weeks; DB 3.3 GB of which 2.9 GB is historical/fd1 identity staging.
findings.impact: Index bloat, slower latest-per-book scans, backup size.
findings.remediation: RECOMMENDED: monthly partitions or 90-day archival for snapshot tables; composite index F51-001.

findings.title: No account deletion/export endpoints, no privacy notice, no age gate or responsible-gaming copy
findings.evidence: OBSERVED: route inventory has no delete/export; UI states research/simulation only and no real-money wagering.
findings.impact: Public launch obligations unmet (requires qualified legal review; not legal advice).
findings.remediation: RECOMMENDED: self-service delete/export, privacy policy, 18+/21+ gate per jurisdiction, responsible-gaming links, no profit guarantees.

findings.title: Client hard-codes sport lists (LeagueCode union, supported_filters literal) alongside the registry it now fetches
findings.evidence: OBSERVED: 932f556 now consumes /sports/registry via useSportRegistry (repairs the earlier duplication), but the TS literal types still enumerate MLB/NFL/NBA/WNBA/UFC and 'ALL'|'MLB'|'NFL'.
findings.impact: Type drift when a sport is promoted.
findings.rootCause: Static typing of a dynamic registry.
findings.remediation: RECOMMENDED: widen to string with runtime validation, or generate types from the OpenAPI schema.
